citations.B1: Read-modify-write on `counts[user_id]` isn't atomic — two threads can both read the same count and both increment, letting requests past the limit
citations.B3: use a per-user lock or an atomic/threadsafe counter (e.g. `collections.Counter` with a lock, or `threading.Lock` around the check-and-increment)
citations.B4: No window/expiry — `count` never resets, so after the first `limit` requests ever, the user is blocked forever
citations.B5: Unbounded memory growth — `counts` grows forever, one entry per distinct `user_id`, never cleaned up
citations.B6: State is per-process only — multiple workers each get their own `counts`, so the real limit is `limit * num_workers`
citations.B7: No validation on `user_id` — `None`, empty, or absent values are silently treated as a valid bucket
